reason: I can write a Playwright script that crawls the sitemap and shoots every page at mobile and desktop sizes in an afternoon, and it runs on our own machines. Nine dollars a month isn't much, but I'd be paying for something I already have.
objection: The login-page feature means pasting a live browser session into a brand-new tool with no reviews. That's basically handing over the keys to our admin. I wouldn't be allowed to do that, and I wouldn't want to. Also, emulated iPhone and Android viewports are not real devices.
would_change_my_mind: If my team needed scheduled visual diffs with email alerts across lots of sites and I had no time to maintain scripts, and it ran self-hosted or never touched session cookies, I might pay for it.
